chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from the one whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The strap of the slipper of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) broke while he was in a funeral. So a man came with his strap to hand it to him He said: 'Hold on to your strap, for the owner of the misfortune is more deserving of patience with it.'

key_terms.شِسْعُ: The strap or thong of a sandal or slipper

ai.seo_question: What is the lesson of patience in misfortune according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this incident from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) demonstrates the virtue of *sabr* (patience) by refusing a replacement strap for his broken slipper during a funeral, teaching that the one enduring the hardship is most deserving of the patience required to bear it. This narrative highlights the Shia emphasis on internal spiritual resilience over external comfort, illustrating how even minor inconveniences serve as opportunities for spiritual refinement and emulation of the Imams' conduct in daily life.

en.hubeali: H 14607 – A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from the one whom he mentioned, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullahasws said, ‘

A strip of the slipper of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> broke whilst he<sup>asws</sup> was in a funeral. So a man came with his strip for his<sup>asws</sup> slipper (as a replacement). He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Hold on to your strip, for the patience is foremost for the people in misfortune’.
